source_span: That rebuild matters because dispersion remains extreme. The 200-day vol of GS TMT Momentum Winners versus Losers is around 76, compared with just 13 for SPX... Net/net: newly rebuilt tech longs are vulnerable to AI and Iran headlines.
source_chain: HFs aggressively rebuilt tech/semis longs at a 97th-percentile two-week pace while broad-index fear stayed low and single-name dispersion stayed extreme (6x SPX vol), THEREFORE those freshly rebuilt longs sat exposed to single-name headline risk with no index-level cushion, THEREFORE Amodei's 'pace the frontier' weekend call plus a Saudi pipeline/Hormuz energy shock hit those names directly and broke NDX/SMH's technical range. Invalidation (Coppersmith): near-term vol makes sense, but only a break in the bigger AI story itself would justify more than that.
pulse_chain: HFs rebuilt TMT/semis longs at a 97th-percentile two-week pace from a 25th-percentile base (repair not chase) while broad-index fear fell, THEREFORE Amodei's weekend essay on slowing AI development hit Asia and Nasdaq futures hard because dispersion means single names move ~6x more violently than the index and nothing was priced at the index level to cushion a headline aimed at exactly those names, THEREFORE banks disagree on what the essay changes (DB: spending shifts to governance since voluntary restraint is unlikely given the company/country race; GS/JPM: buy the dip; MS: political moratorium risk is no longer negligible). Invalidation: if power/land/data-center capacity is still the binding constraint on AI capex, this is a positioning flush; if $SMH keeps sliding toward BTIG's 200-day target (~17% lower), the safety debate has become a spending debate.
why: the pulse reproduces the note's rebuild-plus-dispersion mechanism for why a single essay could break the tape, keeps the same directional headline-to-breakdown sequence, and translates the note's own vol-vs-bigger-story invalidation into a correctly-sourced (BTIG, 16177) technical level rather than swapping in an unargued condition.
